title: Exoplanets, Habitable Zones, and Biosignatures
executive_summary: An exoplanet is a planet outside the Solar System. Over 5,500 exoplanets have been confirmed using transit photometry and radial velocity methods, revealing diverse planetary systems across the galaxy.
image_caption: Artist's impression of TRAPPIST-1e, an Earth-sized exoplanet in the habitable zone.

key_sections.title: The Goldilocks Habitable Zone
key_sections.content: The circumstellar habitable zone (Goldilocks Zone) is the range of orbits around a star where liquid water could exist on a planet's surface under suitable atmospheric pressure.

key_sections.title: Transit Method and Kepler/TESS Missions
key_sections.content: NASA's Kepler and TESS space telescopes discovered thousands of exoplanets by detecting tiny, periodic dips in starlight when a planet transits in front of its parent star.

key_sections.title: Atmospheric Transmission Spectroscopy and Biosignatures
key_sections.content: By analyzing starlight filtered through an exoplanet's atmosphere during transit, space telescopes like JWST detect atmospheric gas signatures such as water vapor, carbon dioxide, methane, and potential biosignatures.
